title: Introduce hierarchical unbiased sampler and soft rollback governor
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: current canary selection uses simple uniform or fixed-reservoir sampling across traffic slices which biases low-traffic routes and underrepresents ephemeral user cohorts. This causes noisy signals and delayed detection for regressions that impact small-but-critical slices. This change introduces a hierarchical unbiased sampler (HUS) that performs two-stage selection: (1) stratified slice sampling with per-slice reservoir priorities proportional to an importance score (SLO weight, revenue, or manual tag) while applying a bias-correction factor to preserve unbiased estimator properties, and (2) within-slice adaptive stochastic subsampling that uses time-decayed counters to keep memory bounded. Motivation and goals: reduce false negatives for slice-specific regressions, improve statistical efficiency (lower variance for the same probe budget), maintain end-to-end unbiasedness for aggregated metric estimates, and enable soft rollback policies that act on probabilistic evidence instead of hard threshold flips. Design summary: the HUS component sits as a sampling layer in the existing probe scheduler and exports per-probe provenance metadata (slice_id, sampling_weight, correction_factor). Metric ingestion computes weighted estimators and a Bayesian credible interval for each metric (latency p50/p95, success-rate, QPS). The soft rollback governor consumes continuous evidence via an exponential moving-LR accumulator: each probe contributes a log-likelihood ratio toward regression vs baseline; the governor computes a posterior probability of regression and triggers staged mitigation when probability crosses alpha soft thresholds (alpha_warn=0.75, alpha_action=0.92) sustained for a grace window. Soft rollback actions include traffic corking (traffic shed percentage), routing fallback to lower-cost model variant, or pausing new canary allocations. Rollout plan: feature gated under runtime flag perf.hus.enabled, enabled first for synthetic probe routes only, ramp to 5% of live canaries for two weeks, and then 25% pending SRE signoff. Backfill: historical probe traces were replayed against HUS in bench harness to estimate variance reduction; we observed median 32% reduction in sample variance for targeted slices and earlier detection (median time-to-detect reduced by 18%). Tests and observability: unit tests for reservoir weighting and correction logic, e2e bench harness comparing bayesian credible intervals to bootstrap baselines, new dashboard panels for sampling weight distribution and posterior probability timeline, and alerting rules for governor state transitions. Migration notes: the sampling is backward compatible since correction_factor is stored on probe metadata and used by the aggregator; if disabled the system falls back to legacy uniform sampling. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2147) [x] Bench harness runs and artifacts uploaded [x] Unit and integration tests added [x] Dashboard and alerting added [x] Rollout plan added. Related: addresses SUP-9421 customer complaint about slice-specific regressions not catching latency spikes.

diff_highlights: hus_sampler.go: ~250 LOC new implementation; core algorithm uses per-slice ring reservoirs and adaptive decay counters
scheduler.go: 2 small integration points to call sampler and attach provenance headers
soft_rollback.go: governor state machine ~120 LOC, supports warn/action thresholds and graceful de-escalation
weighted_estimator.go: new estimator applying correction_factor for unbiased aggregation
review_comments: Miguel Hernandez (review): Overall this looks good and addresses the SUP case. Two items: 1) explain why bias correction preserves unbiased global aggregates when weights change over time, 2) clarify worst-case memory for reservoirs.

Author reply (Aisha): For 1) added a short proof in hus_sampler.go comments and added unit test that replays with dynamic weight changes; For 2) reservoirs use bounded ring buffers with time-decay eviction; worst-case memory = O(num_slices * reservoir_size) and we cap reservoir_size via config per deploy. Expanded README in the package.

Lina Zhang (review): The Bayesian accumulator thresholds feel tuned to bench traces; can we add a conservative default and make them runtime-configurable? Also add a short-circuit to avoid acting on single-probe anomalies.

Author reply (Aisha): Good call. Added governor config for alpha_warn/alpha_action and min_consecutive_evidence parameter; default min_consecutive_evidence=3. Updated tests to cover the short-circuit path.
Ethan Brooks (approver): Verified bench results and tests locally. Left one nit on log verbosity when governor flips state (will follow up in a small logging patch). Approving for merge.

release_notes: Add hierarchical unbiased sampler for canary probes and a probabilistic soft rollback governor. Improves detection sensitivity for small traffic slices and reduces sample variance for targeted probes. Feature gated; disabled by default. See ENG-2147 for rollout plan.
notes_for_sre: Default config kept conservative: reservoir_size=128, min_consecutive_evidence=3, alpha_warn=0.75, alpha_action=0.92. Observe new dashboard panels: Sampling weight distribution and Governor posterior timeline. If governor triggers unexpected actions, flip perf.hus.enabled=false or increase min_consecutive_evidence. Logs emitted under logger=canary.hus and canary.governor.
